title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 5th District
area: South Carolina's 5th Congressional District (north-central South Carolina, including Rock Hill and Sumter)

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Ralph Norman (R) withdrew and did not appear on the June 9, 2026 Republican primary ballot. That primary was then canceled and Wes Climer, a sitting state senator, advanced as the Republican nominee.
Mallory Dittmer won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026 with 55.8% of the vote, defeating Andrew Clough.

candidates.name: Wes Climer
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Wes Climer is a Republican state senator from York County, first elected to the South Carolina Senate in 2016, and the Republican nominee for the open 5th District seat. A financial advisor by trade, he chairs the Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee. According to his campaign website, he is running on cutting taxes, limiting spending and supporting President Trump's agenda.

background.text: Born September 26, 1982, in Charlotte, North Carolina; the state Senate biography lists him as an Eagle Scout, and his campaign website says he was raised in South Carolina.
Earned a B.A. from Furman University in 2006.
According to Wikipedia, worked from 2006 to 2011 as a Washington, D.C.-based congressional aide to Rep. Patrick McHenry and Sens. Elizabeth Dole and Bill Cassidy.
His campaign website describes him as a financial advisor and business owner.

Won the 2016 Republican primary for South Carolina Senate District 15 against incumbent Robert W. Hayes Jr., who had held the seat since 1991, and took office November 14, 2016. He was re-elected in 2020.

Chairs the Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee and also serves on the Family and Veterans' Services, Finance, Labor, Commerce and Industry, Legislative Oversight and Transportation committees.

In June 2025 he and attorney Dick Harpootlian sued the State of South Carolina over the legislature's budget pay raise for lawmakers, which they said violated the state constitution; he declined the additional pay.

Announced his run for the 5th District on July 31, 2025, after Rep. Ralph Norman said he would run for governor; Norman endorsed him on August 21, 2025. The Republican primary on June 9, 2026, was canceled.
According to his campaign website, he is a husband and father of five.

record.text: Chairs the South Carolina Senate's Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee (2025-2026) and serves on the Family and Veterans' Services, Finance, Labor Commerce and Industry, and Transportation committees.

candidates.name: Mallory Dittmer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary (June 9, 2026) with 55.8% of the vote

summary.text: Mallory Dittmer is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's open 5th District seat. A resident of Fort Mill, she worked 15 years in the fashion industry before becoming a business owner, political advocate and founding organizer of a nonpartisan public-education group. According to her campaign materials, she is running on cost of living and bipartisan problem-solving.

background.text: Says she was born and raised in the Midwest, splitting time between her mother's home in a Chicago suburb and her father's family farm in southern Indiana.
Describes a career of about 15 years in the fashion and retail industry, rising to vice president at age 33 and working with brands including Kate Spade and Coach.
After the fashion industry she became a small business owner, according to ABC News 4.
Moved with her husband, Drew, a public school teacher, to Fort Mill, SC, in 2020; they have two children, according to her campaign website.

Is a founding organizer of Community Advocates for Public Education York County, a nonpartisan group supporting public education; in 2024 she managed and supported several local campaigns, helping candidates win seven of nine races, according to ABC News 4 reporting on her campaign announcement.
Announced her candidacy on September 29, 2025. According to WRHI, she opposed the proposed mid-decade congressional redistricting in South Carolina.
Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary over Andrew Clough.

priorities.text: Says the top priority she has heard from voters is the cost of living — groceries, gas, healthcare, and housing — and that she will prioritize economic and trade policies to curb inflation and lower costs.

positions.summary: Says she will support raising the minimum wage.
positions.quote: I'll support raising the minimum wage, making childcare more affordable, reversing cuts to health care programs and lowering housing prices through government programs and tax incentives.

positions.summary: Says she will work to reverse cuts to healthcare programs.
positions.quote: reversing cuts to health care programs
